final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 is the critical negatively charged substrate-binding residue in OCT1; alanine substitution abolishes charge interaction essential for cation transport while preserving protein folding and membrane expression.

R485 is a highly conserved charged residue in the translocation pathway required for transport dynamics; alanine substitution leads to severe loss of transport function while retaining structural integrity.
Neutralizing the D473 carboxylate to asparagine eliminates substrate electrostatics required for transport while maintaining side-chain backbone geometry and protein stability.

stop_reason.detail: The top 3 candidates represent high-confidence functional knockouts supported by mechanistic active site roles and loss-of-function predictions, making further tool evidence unnecessary.

history.rationale: D473 is an essential charge-bearing residue in the central substrate-binding cleft of OCT1 required for organic cation interaction. Alanine substitution neutralizes the charge, severely impairing substrate transport while maintaining structural integrity.
D473 is a highly conserved, essential charge-interaction residue in the substrate-binding cleft of OCT1; mutating to Ala abolishes transport while maintaining overall protein expression.
High AlphaMissense pathogenicity score supports loss of substrate transport function at the primary charge interaction site.
Asparagine substitution at position 473 preserves steric bulk and potential hydrogen bonding while removing the negative charge essential for organic cation binding and translocation.
Asn substitution neutralizes the negative charge of D473 required for cation interaction while preserving side-chain hydrogen bonding capacity to maintain folding.
Charge neutralization at position 473 effectively abolishes organic cation substrate transport.

E488 forms part of the conserved translocating pathway salt-bridge/polar network in SLC22 family transporters. Mutating E488 to alanine disrupts electrostatic substrate interactions without misfolding the protein.
E488 participates in substrate translocation pathways; alanine substitution removes key electrostatic interactions necessary for cation transport.
Very low predicted LOF phenotype indicates transport activity is likely retained.
Glutamine at position 488 neutralizes the conserved carboxylate charge required for substrate translocation while minimizing structural disruption.
Gln substitution neutralizes E488 to severely impair substrate binding while retaining steric bulk and polar contact potential for structural stability.
Benign pathogenicity score indicates retained transport function.
R485 participates in the conserved charge network in the C-terminal translocation channel. Alanine substitution eliminates critical electrostatic interactions required for transport.
R485 forms crucial salt bridges/electrostatic contacts during substrate translocation; mutating to Ala disrupts substrate translocation kinetics.
Highest predicted pathogenicity proxy confirms severe loss of function while maintaining basic structural stability.
D397 is located in TM10 facing the intracellular gate/translocation pathway. Charge removal disrupts ion/substrate coordination and transport kinetics.
D397 resides in the translocation pathway and contributes to substrate specificity; Ala substitution disrupts substrate binding.
Moderate loss of function predicted by AlphaMissense for substrate interaction residue D397.
Isosteric mutation of D397 to asparagine removes the essential negative charge involved in substrate translocation while retaining local hydrogen bonding.
Asn substitution at position 397 eliminates charge interaction necessary for organic cation transport while minimizing folding disruption.
Low pathogenicity score indicates residual transport function, requiring candidate demotion.
D425 resides in TM10 involved in channel lining. Substitution to alanine reduces substrate binding affinity while preserving helical backbone folding.
D425 is located near the pore region; loss of negative charge reduces substrate affinity.
Low LOF phenotype score fails to support target transport ablation.
W216 provides aromatic cation-pi interaction in the substrate-binding pocket. Replacing it with alanine diminishes substrate binding while maintaining overall transmembrane architecture.
W216 provides aromatic/hydrophobic stacking interactions in the central binding cavity; Ala substitution impairs substrate transport.
AlphaMissense supports functional transport ablation upon alanine substitution of key aromatic pocket residue W216.
R171 is part of the conserved MFS intracellular gating motif. Neutralization disrupts substrate transport dynamics while maintaining global fold.
R171 is an essential charged residue in TM4 involved in the transport mechanism.
Moderate pathogenicity score, retaining in mid-tier candidate pool.
